nodes.description: Golgi processing of N-glycans fails, giving accumulation of high-mannose and hybrid structures on secreted glycoproteins together with hyposialylation and hypogalactosylation. The defect is tissue-restricted in a way that is diagnostically and mechanistically informative: serum glycoproteins are grossly abnormal while N-glycans in fibroblasts and undifferentiated iPSC are normal, which points at the liver as the site of disease and rules out a cell-autonomous defect of the glycosylation machinery.

nodes.description: Liver-derived coagulation proteins are deficient, giving a prolonged prothrombin time and activated partial thromboplastin time, hypofibrinogenaemia and severely reduced antithrombin activity. The deficiency is multifactorial and, importantly, is not one-sided: procoagulant factors II and XI fall alongside the anticoagulant antithrombin, so the haemostatic balance is partly preserved and reported patients have tolerated major surgery. That observation rests on a small number of cases and is curated as a treatment consideration, not as an established safety claim.

nodes.description: The recurrent c.1267C>T (p.Arg423*) allele truncates the last seven residues of G6PT1, deleting the C-terminal ER retrieval signal that normally returns the transporter to the endoplasmic reticulum. This is the initiating lesion, and it is a loss of an address label rather than a loss of transport activity.

nodes.description: Freed of its retrieval signal, the truncated transporter moves into the secretory pathway. Its destination is disputed - the Golgi on the original model, a distinct non-Golgi compartment such as ER exit sites on the later one - and the two readings are carried as separate hypothesis groups. The edges out of this node are annotated to both groups because each account produces the same downstream Golgi disturbance.

nodes.description: The mislocalized transporter lowers Golgi intraluminal pH and alters Golgi morphology in a manner that tracks allele dosage. The pH change is the mechanistic hinge: Golgi glycosyltransferases and glycosidases have narrow pH optima, so an acidification shift is sufficient to derange processing without any defect in the glycosylation enzymes themselves. Independent support comes from serum bikunin proteoglycan isoforms, whose esterified heavy forms are known to report Golgi pH and are severely reduced here.
